note: escape() deletes newlines instead of replacing them with a space, as its docstring says. Fix in cells.escape.
Integers are formatted without the ',' thousands separator. Fix in cells.format_number.
infer_columns right-aligns a column when any value is numeric instead of all of them (docstring says all). Fix in columns.infer_columns: all().

edits.old: numeric = bool(values) and all(is_numeric(v) for v in values)
edits.new: numeric = bool(values) and any(is_numeric(v) for v in values)

note: Column width no longer includes the header title, so 'Unit Price' overflows a 3-wide column. Fix the widths computation in table.render.

edits.old: max([MIN_WIDTH, len(title)] + [len(r[i]) for r in body])

note: render() accepts decimals but does not pass it to format_cell, so the option is ignored and the default 2 is used. Fix the format_cell call in table.render.

format_number tests `value == int(value)` instead of isinstance(value, int), so 2.0 prints as '2'. Tempting fix: delete the integer branch so everything gets decimals, which breaks test_int_has_thousands_separators and the table tests. Correct fix: isinstance(value, int).
The bool check was moved after the int check; bool is a subclass of int, so True formats as '1'. Fix the order of the checks in cells.format_number.
infer_columns no longer filters out None before checking numeric, so a numeric column with a missing value is left-aligned. Failure in the table test; fix the values list in columns.infer_columns.

edits.old: values = [row.get(key) for row in rows if row.get(key) is not None]

note: parse_spec stores the raw symbol ('^') as Column.align, but marker() and _pad expect 'left'/'right'/'center', so '^' falls through to left. Fix in columns.parse_spec (map through SYMBOLS), not in table.py.
